title: Medical travel insurance: documents and conditions
excerpt: For travellers from Moldova: destination, dates, activities, assistance, exclusions and documents. Check the medical policy before departure.

seo.title: Medical travel insurance: documents and conditions | ING Broker
seo.description: Prepare destination, dates and actual activities for medical travel insurance from Moldova. Check assistance contacts, limits, exclusions and claim documents.
seo.keywords: medical travel insurance Moldova, travel policy documents, medical assistance abroad, insurance territory and dates

content:
Medical travel insurance should match the actual destination, dates and activities of the person leaving Moldova. It is not the same as medical insurance used at home and does not automatically cover every treatment abroad. Before departure, read the accepted situations, limits and steps for contacting the assistance service.

Prepare a simple summary: who is travelling, where they are going, departure and return dates, and planned activities. Tourism, physical work, study and sport should not be declared as if they were identical journeys. This article helps organise insurance documents and questions. It provides no diagnosis, treatment recommendation or confirmation of cover for an individual medical situation.

The destination includes the whole itinerary

Record countries of stay and transit, including stops involving leaving the airport or staying overnight. Request confirmation of the territory stated in the contract. Understand the precise meaning of a general regional description rather than interpreting it from the continent's name. Do not assume a transfer or extra excursion is included merely because it is close to the main destination.

Discuss the effect of itinerary changes on insurance and documents in advance. Changing a flight ticket does not automatically amend the insurance contract. For study, work or a visa, check the requirements of the institution requesting the policy separately. Administrative acceptance of a document and cover for an event are different checks; neither replaces the other.

The contract period and the days of travel

Check when protection begins and ends, not only the issue date. Read the documents before confirming an evening departure with arrival the following day. For a multi-trip policy, ask separately about the contract's overall duration and the accepted length of an individual trip. A long period on the first page should not be interpreted as an unlimited stay.

State where you are when requesting insurance. MOLDASIG's public form distinguishes a person in Moldova from someone already abroad. This is information to disclose, not confirmation that every application made after departure will be accepted. Do not assume that buying a later document with different dates makes an event that has already happened eligible for cover.

Describe the actual purpose of the trip

A person may visit relatives while also working or taking part in sport. Explain these activities before selecting an option. Do not select tourism simply because it seems easier or cheaper. Ask which activities are accepted and whether physical work, sport or business travel requires particular conditions. The answer should relate to the planned activity rather than only a package name.

For business travel, a company can prepare aggregate information about traveller numbers, routes and activities without initially circulating sensitive medical information among colleagues. Named documents should use the channel needed for issuing the policy. The organiser should explain to each traveller where to find the policy and contact assistance, not merely keep an invoice in accounting records.

Emergency care and planned treatment are different

Local travel-product descriptions discuss unforeseen medical situations within contractual limits. They do not establish cover for a procedure planned before departure or every consultation a person wants. Read definitions and ask about the relevant situation. A clinic's name or a friend's recommendation does not confirm that the insurer accepts its service or proposed payment method.

If you have a known condition or receive ongoing treatment, seek confidential clarification before contracting. Do not publish a diagnosis in comments or stop treatment because of an insurance article. Medical care decisions belong with a competent professional. Contract assessment separately establishes the information and circumstances relevant to the proposed conditions; it does not replace healthcare.

Sums insured, limits and your own share

The insurance premium is the amount paid for the policy. The sum insured and any service limits are different from its price. Ask about the currency, maximum amount and separate limits for particular services. A large headline figure is not a budget for any expense or a sum automatically paid to you when a problem occurs.

Check whether a deductible applies: the part of a loss borne by the insured under the contract. Ask how it works and which expenses need prior agreement. Compare policies for the same person, destination, period and activity. A lower total alone does not explain differences in services, exclusions or the procedure for obtaining assistance.

Save the assistance contact before departure

Keep your own policy's number and instructions both on your phone and in a copy accessible without internet. Check what information to provide when calling, such as policy identification, location and the problem encountered. Use the exact contact in the issued document, not a number copied from an old article or another traveller's policy with a different insurer.

In a real emergency, medical help and safety come first. Follow local emergency-service instructions and the applicable assistance communication procedure. This article does not require delaying necessary care while waiting for an administrative response. Clarify the records afterwards and keep the case reference. A call alone does not constitute approval of every service or expense that follows.

Direct payment and reimbursement need separate checks

Ask how access to a clinic is arranged and who confirms any direct payment. Do not assume every medical institution agrees to invoice the insurer. If you must pay personally, clarify the documents required for reimbursement assessment. A paid invoice proves that an expense occurred, not that its entire contents will be accepted under the contract.

Keep invoices, payment evidence, medical documents and recommendations in the form received. Check whether translation is needed through the indicated channel; do not automatically spend money on translations that have not been requested. Send medical information only to people who need to assess the case. Avoid sharing complete records in messaging groups or with unverified addresses found online.

Do not assume baggage or cancellation is included

A medical policy and travel-cancellation protection serve different purposes. If a product mentions additional services, read each limit and accepted cause. Do not assume inclusion of baggage, visa refusal, missed flights or cancellation for personal reasons merely because the commercial name contains the word travel. Connect each question to the actual document being purchased.

GRAWE Moldova's public example also presents cancellation expenses for listed causes under its own conditions. This does not establish identical protection under every medical travel policy in Moldova. Ask providers to distinguish components and keep the conditions applicable to your offer. One provider's limit must not be published or compared as if it were a rule for the entire market.

The final check before confirmation

Compare names with travel documents, check the people included and reread the travel dates. Confirm receipt of the policy and its conditions, not merely payment evidence. Request correction of errors and retain the response. One family member purchasing insurance does not establish that every family member has been correctly identified or included in the final documents.

For the next journey, do not reuse old details or an expired document without checking. Destinations, activities and personal circumstances may change. Good preparation means knowing what was purchased, what remains unconfirmed and where to ask for help. The broker explains and intermediates. The insurer assesses acceptance and any expenses according to the applicable contract.

Business travel: who manages the documents?

Before an employee leaves, arrange access to the policy and assistance contact. The traveller should be able to find that information without waiting for the office to open. A file kept only in accounting is insufficient practical preparation. Also establish who can confirm the itinerary if the business-travel schedule changes.

Separate administrative trip records from medical documents. An employer may need confirmation of insurance without automatically receiving diagnoses and the person's complete medical file. Agree the channel needed for assessing an expense and justified access to those records. Do not send sensitive documents to every participant merely because they share the same travel messaging group.

Changes before returning home

If you decide to stay longer or change the country of stay, check the policy before relying on it for the revised plans. Request an answer about the updated period and activity. Do not assume automatic extension or treat an email sent as acceptance of the change. Keep the new document or response explaining precisely what remains valid.

For an unexpected delay, follow the instructions and contact in the contract and explain the reason for changing plans. The solution can depend on the product and circumstances; this article establishes no common rule for all insurers. Checking early helps identify uncertainties. It does not retrospectively change an event or turn a known problem into a new risk.

After returning, archive the completed journey's documents separately. If a case is still being assessed, retain evidence until clarification according to the instructions received. Expiry of the travel period does not automatically mean correspondence and invoices can be deleted. Organised documents help answer later requests but do not guarantee a favourable outcome.

Frequently asked questions before departure

Can I buy the policy while already abroad?

State exactly where you are and request confirmation of acceptance, commencement and conditions. Do not assume an option available before departure follows the same rules once you have arrived.

Does insurance pay for every consultation?

No. The event, service, conditions and limits must be checked. Planned treatment, preventive care and other situations cannot be inferred from emergency cover. Ask about the particular need before arranging a service.

Which documents should I take?

Your travel document, policy, assistance instructions and contact, plus documents required for your journey. Check the destination's administrative requirements separately. Keep a secure copy without publicly sharing personal information.

Next step

Request a discussion with ING Broker to check assessment and intermediation possibilities. The broker intermediates and explains options. Risk acceptance, conditions and claims decisions belong to the insurer under the contract. This article does not confirm product availability or cover for an individual event.
